film: CANYON RAIL: first 10 s of a railroad short, recreated through the hybrid pipeline (Phase 8 second-script test; the script is read from a reference short's captions, not fact-checked)

s01_start.rationale: Engineer is large, clear and on-model with the toothy grin, but the handcar is a blurred, half-occluded dark sliver behind his legs and the red-yellow canyon wall dominates; the 'size is the joke' premise is not staged.
s01_start.fix: Pull the camera back to a low three-quarter wide so the full handcar and the rails sit sharp beside the engineer, and cut the depth-of-field blur on the car.

s01_end.rationale: Sunglasses-and-hammer pose is a fun, readable beat with the hammer in hand, but the handcar is cropped at the right edge and softened, so the tool-plus-car story is only half told.
s01_end.fix: Shift the engineer left and the handcar right so the whole car, with its red beam, is in frame and in focus.

s02_start.rationale: Handcar is more visible here (glowing lantern, red walking beam, plank deck), but it is cut off at the left edge, the engineer stands in front of it rather than kneeling at work, and the green water-tower blob competes for attention.
s02_start.fix: Keep the whole car in frame at three-quarter view with the engineer kneeling at the wheel, and drop or desaturate the green background shape.

s02_end.rationale: Near-duplicate of s02_start with a one-eye squint and a small point; the cropped handcar adds nothing new, and the beat that should turn the claim ('39 feet') shows no scale payoff.
s02_end.fix: Make this a distinct payoff frame: pointing up at the bridge with the whole car and a rail gauge in frame to set scale.

s03_start.rationale: Abstract blurred low-angle shot of a grey beam, a lattice and a blue block; it does not read as a bridge or a canyon, there is no hero, and it is orange and grey mush at phone size.
s03_start.fix: Reframe as a clear upward shot from the track showing a recognisable high trestle across the canyon sky, with the engineer's silhouette in the foreground looking up.

s03_end.rationale: Same muddy look-up as the start with a slight camera drift; depth and height are hinted at but not sold, and the framing is dominated by a flat grey slab.
s03_end.fix: Push the camera so the bridge deck's underside and far abutment are sharp, and add a rail or ladder cue for scale.

s04_start.rationale: Practically identical to s03_end (same lattice, same wall) so the last beat has no new picture, no hero, and no handcar; the ending does not land.
s04_start.fix: Cut to a hero-and-bridge payoff: the engineer small in the lower frame, the tall bridge towering over him, as the final image.

s04_end.rationale: Byte-for-byte the same frame as s04_start, a static empty canyon look-up with no character or story information; the film ends on a still wallpaper.
s04_end.fix: Add a camera move or a final character reaction so the end frame differs from the start frame and holds the payoff.

char_eng.rationale: Stationmaster is consistent across front, three-quarter, side and back views and the expression cards (grin, squint, sunglasses), uniform matches the locked cast and he reads at phone size; the required kneel_work pose is not seen on the sheet or in the panels, and the point_out pose is barely visible.
char_eng.fix: Add and show a kneel_work card, and a clear point_out pose with a visible hammer, then stage them in s02 and s03.

asset_prop_rail_handcar.rationale: Identity and colours hold up (plank deck, red walking beam, dark frame, glowing lantern on a pole, spoked flanged wheels, a scale that is plausible against the engineer), but at 720x1280 it is always partly cropped, blurred or behind his legs, its toolbox and name plate cannot be read, and the best view (s02) still crops a wheel; the three-quarter silhouette promised by the requirement never gets its own clean frame.
asset_prop_rail_handcar.fix: Add one clean three-quarter hero frame of the full handcar on the rails with the engineer kneeling beside it, sharp focus and rim-lit, so the beam, lantern, toolbox and wheels are readable and the 1.37 m scale is obvious.

film_level.notes: The strong half is the first two beats: the engineer is on-model, charming and consistent, and the handcar's colours and identity are right. But the handcar is repeatedly cropped, blurred or occluded and never given a clean readable frame. The back half (s03 and s04) is two near-identical, muddy look-up shots of grey lattice and orange rock with no hero, no readable bridge and no handcar, so the story ('looks up at the high bridge') and the scale joke never pay off. s04_start and s04_end are the same image. Panels average well under 8.5.

studio_director.note: Send back. Re-stage so the full handcar sits sharp and uncropped beside a kneeling or pointing engineer with a visible rail gauge; replace s03 and s04 with a legible high-bridge reveal featuring the hero, and make the end frame differ from the start frame. Drop the heavy depth-of-field blur and the distracting green blob.
